chapters: And in the first year of Koresh, the king of Paras, at the completion of the word of Havayah from the mouth of Yirmeyah, Havayah aroused the Spirit of Koresh, the king of Paras, and he issued a proclamation throughout his kingdom, and also in writing, saying:
"So Koresh said, the king of Paras, 'All the kingdoms of the Earth Havayah Elokim of the heavens delivered to me, and He commanded me to build Him a House in Yerushalayim, which is in Yehudah.

Who is among you of all His people, may his Elokim be with him, and he may ascend to Yerushalayim, which is in Yehudah, and let him build the House of Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel; He is the Elokim Who is in Yerushalayim.

And whoever remains from all the places where he sojourns, the people of his place shall help him with silver and with gold and with possessions and with cattle, with the donation to the House of Elokim, which is in Yerushalayim.'
And the heads of the families of Yehudah and Binyamin and the priests and the Leviim arose, with all whom Elokim inspired to ascend to build the House of Havayah, which is in Yerushalayim.
And all those around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with possessions, with cattle, and with precious things, besides all that was donated.
And King Koresh took out all the vessels of the House of Havayah, which Nevuchadnezzar had taken out of Yerushalayim and had placed them in the temple of his god.
Now Koresh, the king of Paras, took them out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and he counted them out to Sheishbatzar, the prince of Yehudah.
And these are their number: thirty basins of gold, a thousand basins of silver, twenty-nine knives,
Thirty bowls of gold, secondary silver bowls four hundred and ten, a thousand other vessels.
All the vessels of silver and gold were five thousand, four hundred; Sheishbatzar brought up everything when the exiles were brought up from Bavel to Yerushalayim.

And these are the people of the province who went up from the captivity of the exile, whom Nevuchadnezzar, the king of Bavel, had exiled to Bavel, and they returned to Yerushalayim and Yehudah, each one to his city.
[Those] who came with Zerubavel, Yeshua, Nechemiah, Serayah, Reelayah, Mordechai Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvei, Rechum, Baanah, the number of the important men of the people of Yisroel.
The children of Parosh were two thousand, one hundred seventy-two.
The children of Shefatyah were three hundred seventy-two.
The children of Arah were seven hundred seventy-five.
The children of Pahath-Moav, of the children of Yeshua [and] Yoav, were two thousand eight hundred and twelve.
The children of Eilam were a thousand two hundred fifty-four.
The children of Zattu were nine hundred forty-five.
The children of Zakkai were seven hundred and sixty.
The children of Bani were six hundred forty-two.
The children of Bebai were six hundred twenty-three.
The children of Azgad were a thousand two hundred twenty-two.
The children of Adonikam were six hundred sixty-six.
The children of Bigvai were two thousand fifty-six.
The children of Adin were four hundred fifty-four.
The children of Ater, of Chizkiyah, were ninety-eight.
The children of Bezai were three hundred twenty-three.
The children of Yorah were a hundred and twelve.
The children of Chusham were two hundred twenty-three.
The children of Gibbar were ninety-five.
The children of Beis Lechem were a hundred twenty-three.
The people of Netofah were fifty-six.
The people of Anatot were a hundred twenty-eight.
The children of Azmaveth were forty-two.
The children of Kiryas-Arim, Kefirah, and Beeroth were seven hundred forty-three.
The children of Ramah and Geva were six hundred twenty-one.
The people of Michmas were a hundred twenty-two.
The people of Beis El and Ai were two hundred twenty-three.
The children of Nebo were fifty-two.
The children of Magbish were a hundred fifty-six.
The children of the other Eilam were a thousand two hundred fifty-four.
The children of Harim were three hundred and twenty.
The children of Lod, Hadid, and Ono were seven hundred twenty-five.
The children of Yericho were three hundred forty-five.
The children of Senaah were three thousand six hundred and thirty.
The priests: the children of Yedayah, of the house of Yeshua, were nine hundred seventy-three.
The children of Immer were a thousand fifty-two.
The children of Pashhur were a thousand two hundred and forty-seven.
The children of Harim were a thousand and seventeen.
The Leviim: the children of Yeshua and Kadmiel, of the children of Hodavyah, were seventy-four.
The singers: the children of Asaf were a hundred twenty-eight.

The children of the gatekeepers: the children of Shalum, the children of Ater, the children of Talmon, the children of Akkub, the children of Hatita, the children of Shobai, in all a hundred thirty-nine.
The Nethinim: the children of Ziha, the children of Hasupha, the children of Tabbaoth.
The children of Keros, the children of Siaha, the children of Padon.
The children of Lebanah, the children of Hagabah, the children of Akkub.
The children of Hagab, the children of Salmai, the children of Chanan.
The children of Giddel, the children of Gahar, the children of Reayah.
The children of Rezin, the children of Nekoda, the children of Gazzam.
The children of Uzza, the children of Paseah, the children of Besai.
The children of Asnah, the children of Meunim, the children of Nephusim.
The children of Bakbuk, the children of Hakupha, the children of Harhur.
The children of Bazluth, the children of Mehida, the children of Harsha.
The children of Barkos, the children of Sisra, the children of Tamah.
The children of Netziach, the children of Hatifa.
The children of Shlomo's slaves, the children of Sotai, the children of Hassophereth, the children of Peruda.
The children of Yalach, the children of Darkon, the children of Giddel.
The children of Shefatyah, the children of Hattil, the children of Pochereth Hazzebaim, the children of Ami.
All the Nethinim and the children of Shlomo's slaves were three hundred ninety-two.
And these were the ones who ascended from Tel-Melah, Tel-Harsha: Keruv, Addan, [and] Immer; but they could not tell their fathers' house and their children, if they were from Yisroel.
The children of Delayah, the children of Toviyah, the children of Nekoda were six hundred fifty-two.
And of the children of the priests: the children of Chovayah, the children of Hakkoz, the children of Barzilai who took a wife of the daughters of Barzilai the Giladis and was called by their name.
These who traced their genealogy sought their records, but they were not found, and they were disqualified from the priesthood.
And Hatirshasa said to them that they should not eat of the most holy sacrifices until a priest arises for the Urim and the Tumim.
The entire congregation together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty.
Besides their slaves and their bondwomen; these were seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven, and they had two hundred male and female singers.
Their horses were seven hundred thirty-six, their mules were two hundred forty-five.
Their camels were four hundred thirty-five, donkeys six thousand seven hundred and twenty.
And of the heads of the fathers' houses, when they came to the House of Havayah, which was in Yerushalayim, they donated to the House of Elokim to erect it on its foundation.
According to their ability, they gave to the treasury of the work; gold, sixty-one thousand drachmas, and silver, five thousand manehs and a hundred priests' tunics.
And the priests, the Leviim, and of the people, and the singers, the gatekeepers, and the Nethinim, dwelt in their cities, and all Yisroel in their cities.
The seventh month arrived, and the Children of Yisroel [were] in the cities, and the people gathered like one man to Yerushalayim.

And Yeshua the son of Yehozadak arose, and his brethren the priests, and Zerubavel the son of Shealtiel, and his brethren, and they built the altar of the Elokim of Yisroel, upon which to offer up burnt offerings, as it is written in the Torah of Moshe, the man of Elokim.

And they set the altar on its bases, for because of the fear that was upon them from the people of the lands, they offered up burnt offerings to Havayah, burnt offerings for the morning and for the evening.
And they observed the feast of Succoth as is written, and the burnt offering of each day in its day, in the number, as the ordinance of each day in its day.

And afterwards [they offered] the daily burnt offering, and for the New Moon and for all the appointed seasons of Havayah that were hallowed, and for everyone who willingly offered a free — will offering to Havayah.
From the first day of the seventh month they commenced to offer up burnt offerings to Havayah, but the foundation of the Temple of Havayah was not yet laid.

And they gave money to the quarriers and to the artisans, and food and drink and oil to the Tzidonim and to the Tzorim to bring cedar wood from Levanon to the sea of Yafo, by the sanction of Koresh the king of Paras upon them.

And in the second year of their coming to the House of Elokim, to Yerushalayim, in the second month, Zerubavel the son of Shealtiel, and Yeshua, the son of Yehotzadak, and the rest of their brethren, the priests, the Leviim, and all who came from the captivity to Yerushalayim commenced, and they stationed the Leviim from twenty years old and above to conduct the work of the House of Havayah.

And Yeshua, his sons, and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Yehudah, stood together to conduct the ones who did the work in the House of Elokim, the children of Henadad, their sons, and their brothers, the Leviim.

And the builders laid the foundation of the Temple of Havayah, and they stationed the priests in their attire with trumpets, and the Leviim, the sons of Asaf, with cymbals, to praise Havayah through Dovid the king of Yisroel.

And they sang aloud with praise and with thanks to Havayah for it is good, for His kindness is eternal over Yisroel, and the entire people shouted with a great shout with praise to Havayah because the foundation of the House of Havayah was laid.

And many of the priests and the Leviim and the heads of the fathers' houses, old men who had seen the first Temple when its foundation was laid, [when they saw] this Temple with their eyes, were weeping with a loud voice, and many with a shout of joy to raise [their] voice.
And the people did not recognize the voice of the shout of joy because of the voice of the people's weeping, for the people were shouting a great shout, and the voice was heard from afar.
Now the adversaries of Yehudah and Binyamin heard that the people of the exile were building a Temple for Havayah Elokim of Yisroel.

And they approached Zerubavel and the heads of the fathers' houses and said to them, "Let us build with you, for like you we seek your Elokim, and we have been sacrificing to Him since the days of Esarhaddon, the king of Ashur, who brought us up here."

And Zerubavel, Yeshua, and the rest of the heads of the fathers' houses of Yisroel said to them, "It is not for you and for us to build a House for our Elokim, but we ourselves shall build for Havayah Elokim of Yisroel, as King Koresh, the king of Paras, commanded us."
And the people of the land were hindering the people of Yehudah and frightening them from building.
And they would hire advisors against them to frustrate their plan, all the days of Koresh, the king of Paras, and until the kingdom of Daryavesh, the king of Paras.
And in the reign of Achashveirosh, in the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the dwellers of Yehudah and Yerushalayim.

And in the days of Artachshasta, Mithredath Tabeel and the rest of his colleagues wrote with peace, to Artachshasta, the king of Paras, and the script of the epistle was written in Aramaic and explained in Aramaic.
Rechum was the secretary, and Shimshai was the scribe; they wrote a letter about Yerushalayim to Artachshasta the king, as is stated.

Then Rechum the secretary and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their companies, the Dinim, the Apharesattechim, the Tarpelim, the Apharesim, the Archevim, the Bavlim, the Shushanchim, the Dehim, the Eilamim.
And the rest of the nations whom the great and honored Asenappar exiled and settled in the cities of Shomron and the rest of the other side of the river and Ke'eneth.
This is the meaning of the letter that they sent to him, to Artachshasta the king: "Your servants are the people of the other side of the river and Ke'eneth.

Let it be known to the king that the Yehudim who ascended from you upon us have come to Yerushalayim, the rebellious and sinful city they are building, and the walls they have completed, and the walls they have joined.

Now let it be known to the king that if this city is built and the walls are founded, they will not give the king's due, the head tax, or the meal tax they will not give, and the tax of the kings will suffer.
Now, in view of this, that we wish to destroy the Temple, and it is improper for us to witness the king's disgrace, we have therefore sent and notified the king.

That one should search in the annals of your fathers, and you will find in the annals, and you will know that this city is a rebellious city, and it injures kings and countries, and they have made rebellion in its midst since days of yore; because of this, this city was destroyed.
We make known to the king that if this city is built, and its walls founded, because of this, you will have no part in the other side of the river."
The king sent a word to Rechum the secretary and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their companies who lived in Shomron, and the rest of the other side of the river, Shelam and Ke'eth.
"The letter that you sent to us was explained and read before me.
And the order was given by me, and they searched and found that this city had raised itself up over kings, and rebellion and disobedience were committed within it.
And mighty kings were over Yerushalayim who ruled over all beyond the river, and the king's due, the head tax, and the meal tax was given to them.
Now issue an order to stop these men, and this city shall not be built; until orders are given by me.
And beware of committing an error in this matter. Why should the damage increase to injure the kings?"

Then, since the interpretation of the letter of Artachshasta the king was read before Rechum, and Shimshai the scribe, and their companies, they went in haste to Yerushalayim to the Yehudim, and they stopped them with force and might.
Then the work of the House of Elokim, which was in Yerushalayim, was stopped, and it was suspended until the second year of the reign of Daryavesh, the king of Paras.
Now the prophets, Chagai the prophet and Zecharyah, the son of Iddo, prophesied to the Yehudim who were in Yehudah and Yerushalayim, in the Name of the Elokim of Yisroel to them.

Then Zerubavel, the son of Shealtiel and Yeshua, the son of Yehotzadak arose and commenced to build the House of Elokim, which is in Yerushalayim, and with them were the prophets of Elokim assisting them.

At that time, there came upon them Tatnay, the governor of the other side of the river, and Shethar-Bozenai, and their companies, and so they said to them, "Who issued to you the authorization to build this House and to found these walls?"
Then, as we will say, they said to them, "What are the names of the men who are constructing this building?"
And the eye of their Elokim was on the elders of the Yehudim, and they did not stop them until the matter came to Daryavesh, and then they would answer the letter concerning this.

The interpretation of the letter that Tatnay, the governor of the other side of the river, and Shethar-Bozenai, and his companies, the Apharsechim, who are on the other side of the river, sent to King Daryavesh.
They sent a word to him, and so it was written in it: "To King Daryavesh, all peace.

Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Yehudah, to the House of the great Elokim, and it is built of marble, and wood is laid in the walls, and this work was done quickly, and they succeeded with it.
Then we asked these elders; as follows we said to them, 'Who issued to you the authorization to build this House and to finish this wall?'
We also asked them their names, to let you know, that we should write the names of the men who are at their head.

And as follows, they gave us a reply, saying, 'We are servants of the Elokim of heaven and earth, and we are building the House that was built many years before this, and a great king of Yisroel built it and founded it.

But now, since our forefathers angered the Elokim of heaven, He delivered them into the hands of Nevuchadnezzar, the king of Bavel, the Kasdi, and he destroyed this House and exiled the people to Bavel.
But in the first year of Koresh, the king of Bavel, King Koresh issued an order to build this House of Elokim.

And also the vessels of the House of Elokim, of gold and silver, that Nevuchadnezzar had taken out of the Temple that was in Yerushalayim and brought them to the temple of Bavel, King Koresh took them from the temple of Bavel and gave them to one whose name is Sheishbatzar, whom he appointed governor.
And he said to him, 'Take these vessels, go, bring them down into the Temple that is in Yerushalayim, and the House of Elokim shall be built on its place.'
Then this Sheishbatzar came and began building the walls of the House of Elokim that is in Yerushalayim, and from then until now, it is built but not completed.

And now, if it pleases the king, let the royal archives that are there in Bavel be searched, whether it is so that permission was issued by King Koresh to build this House of Elokim in Yerushalayim, and the will of the king concerning this he shall send to us."
Then King Daryavesh gave an order, and they searched in the library in which the archives were stored in Bavel.
And there was found in a pouch in the citadel of the province of Madai one scroll, and so was written therein a memorandum:

In the first year of King Koresh, King Koresh gave an order regarding the House of Elokim in Yerushalayim, that the House should be built, a place where they offer up sacrifices, and its walls should be founded, its height sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits.
Three rows of marble and a row of new wood, and the expenditures shall be given from the royal house.

And also the vessels of the House of Elokim, of gold and silver, which Nevuchadnezzar took out of the Temple that is in Yerushalayim and brought to Bavel, let them be given over and brought to the Temple that is in Yerushalayim to its place, and they shall be deposited in the House of Elokim.
"Now Tatnay, the governor of the other side of the river, Shethar-Bozenai, and their companies, the Apharsechim, who are on the other side of the river, distance yourselves from there.
Leave the work of this House of Elokim; [to] the governors of the Yehudim, and [to] the elders of the Yehudim, [I command] this House of Elokim they shall build in its place.

And from me shall be issued an order regarding what you shall do with these elders of the Yehudim to build this House of Elokim, and from the king's property from the taxes of the other side of the river [it shall] quickly [be built.] The expenses shall be given to these men so that they should not be disrupted.

And what they require, and young bulls, and rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the Elokim of the heavens, wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the statement of the priests who are in Yerushalayim, let it be given to them daily without delay.
That they should offer up pleasing sacrifices to the Elokim of heaven and pray for the lives of the king and his children.

And an order is issued by me that whatever person disobeys this order, a beam shall be torn from his house, and a gallows [shall be made], upon which to place him, and his house shall be made a dungheap because of this.

And Elokim, Who caused His name to rest there, will cast down any king or people that lays a hand to alter and destroy this House of Elokim, which is in Yerushalayim; I, Daryavesh, have issued an edict; it shall be swiftly executed."
Then, Tatnay, the governor of the land beyond the river, Shethar-Bozenai, and their companies, in view of what King Daryavesh had sent, as was said, acted swiftly.

And the elders of the Yehudim were building and succeeding with the prophecy of Chagai the prophet and Zecharyah, the son of Iddo, and they built and founded it by the command of the Elokim of Yisroel and by the command of Koresh, Daryavesh, and Artachshasta, the king of Paras.
And the completion of this House was on the third day of the month of Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of King Daryavesh.
And the Children of Yisroel, the priests, the Leviim, and the rest of the members of the exile, performed the dedication of this House of Elokim with joy.

And they offered up for the dedication of this House of Elokim a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and twelve he-goats for sin-offerings for all Yisroel, according to the number of the tribes of Yisroel.
Now they set up the priests in their divisions and the Leviim in their classes over the service of Elokim, which was in Yerushalayim, as is written in the Book of Moshe.
Now the people of the exile made the Passover [offering] on the fourteenth of the first month.

For the priests and the Leviim purified themselves as one, so they were all pure; and they slaughtered the Passover [offering] for all the people of the exile, and for their brethren, the priests, and for themselves.
And the Children of Yisroel, who had returned from the exile, and whoever separated from the defilement of the nations of the land, to seek Havayah Elokim of Yisroel, partook [of it].

And they celebrated the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy, for Havayah made them joyful and turned the heart of the king of Ashur toward them to strengthen their hands in the work of the House of Elokim, the Elokim of Yisroel.
And after these incidents, in the kingdom of Artachshasta, the king of Paras, Ezra, the son of Serayah, the son of Azaryah, the son of Chilkiyah.
The son of Shalum, the son of Tzadok, the son of Ahitub.
The son of Amaryah, the son of Azaryah, the son of Meraioth.
The son of Zerachyah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki.
The son of Abishua, the son of Pinchas, the son of Elazar, the son of Aharon, the chief priest.

This Ezra ascended from Bavel, and he was a fluent scholar in the Law of Moshe, which Havayah Elokim of Yisroel had given, and the king granted him his entire request, according to the command of Havayah his Elokim upon him.
And there ascended from the Children of Yisroel, from the priests, and the Leviim, and the singers, and the gate-keepers, and the Nethinim to Yerushalayim in the seventh year of King Artachshasta.
And he came to Yerushalayim in the fifth month, which was in the seventh year of the king.
For on the first of the first month was the commencement of the ascent from Bavel, and on the first of the fifth month, he arrived to Yerushalayim according to the good hand of his Elokim upon him.
For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the Law of Havayah and to perform and teach in Yisroel statute and ordinance.
And this is the interpretation of the writ that King Artachshasta gave to Ezra the priest, the scholar, the scholar of the words of Havayah's commandments and His statutes to Yisroel.
"Artachshasta, king of the kings, to Ezra the priest, the scholar who has mastered the Book of the Law of the Elokim of heaven, and Ke'eneth.
An order is issued by me that whoever of my kingdom of the people of Yisroel, its priests and Leviim, who volunteers to go to Yerushalayim with you, may go.
Because of this, before the king and his seven advisors you are sent to search out Yehudah and Yerushalayim according to the law of your Elokim, which is in your hand.
And to bring silver and gold that the king and his advisors donated to the Elokim of Yisroel, Whose habitation is in Yerushalayim.

And all the silver and gold that you will find in the entire province of Bavel, with the donation of the people and the priests, which they are donating to the House of their Elokim, which is in Yerushalayim.

Because of this, you shall quickly purchase with this money bulls, rams, lambs, and their meal-offerings, and their libations, and offer them up on the altar of the House of your Elokim, which is in Yerushalayim.
And what pleases you and your brethren to do with the rest of the silver and gold, as your Elokim wishes, you shall do.
And the vessels that are given to you for the service of the House of your Elokim, give in their entirety before the Elokim [in] Yerushalayim.
And the rest of the necessities of the House of your Elokim, which will fall to you to give, you shall give from the royal treasury.

And from me-I, King Artachshasta is issued forth an edict to all the treasurers who are on the other side of the river, that whatever Ezra, the priest, the scholar of the Law of the Elokim of heaven, requests of you shall be done quickly.
Until a hundred talents of silver, and until a hundred kors of wheat, and until a hundred baths of wine, and until a hundred baths of oil, and salt, [whose amount] is not written.
Whatever is with the authorization of the Elokim of heaven shall be done with a seal for the House of the Elokim of heaven, for why should there be wrath against the realm of the king and his sons?

And we are making known to you that [as regards] all the priests, and the Leviim, the musicians, the gatekeepers, the Nethinim, and those who serve in this House of Elokim — no one should be empowered to levy the king's due, the head tax, or the meal tax upon them.

And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your Elokim, which is in your hand, appoint judges and magistrates who will judge all the people beyond the river, all who know the laws of your Elokim, and whoever does not know, you shall teach them.
And whoever does not fulfill the law of your Elokim and the law of the king promptly-judgment shall be inflicted upon him; whether to be executed, uprooted, fined, or tortured."
Blessed be Havayah, the Elokim of our forefathers, Who put such a thought into the king's heart, to glorify the House of Havayah, which is in Yerushalayim.

And upon me He extended kindness before the king and his advisers, and to all the mighty officers of the king, and I strengthened myself according to the hand of Havayah my Elokim upon me, and I gathered from Yisroel chiefs to go up with me.
And these are the heads of their father's houses and the lineage of those who ascended with me in the kingdom of King Artachshasta from Bavel.
Of the sons of Pinchas, Gershom: of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; of the sons of Dovid, Hattush.
Of the sons of Shechanyah, of the sons of Parosh, Zecharyah, and with him one hundred and fifty males traced their lineage.
Of the sons of Pahath-Moav, Eliehoenai the son of Zerachyah, and with him two hundred males.
Of the sons of Shechanyah, the son of Yahaziel, and with him three hundred males.
And of the sons of Adin, Ebed the son of Yonasan, and with him fifty males.
And of the sons of Eilam, Yeshayah the son of Atalyah, and with him seventy males.
And of the sons of Shefatyah, Zevadyah the son of Michoel, and with him eighty males.
Of the sons of Yoav, Ovadyah the son of Yechiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen males.
And of the sons of Shelomis, the son of Yosephyah, and with him a hundred and sixty males.
And of the sons of Bebai, Zecharyah the son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight males.
And of the sons of Azgad, Yochanan the son of Hakkatan, and with him a hundred and ten males.
And of the sons of Adonikam the last ones, and these are their names: Eliphelet, Yeiel, and Shemayah, and with them were sixty males.
And of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zaccur, and with them were seventy males.
And I gathered them to the flowing river, to Ahavah, and we encamped there for three days, and I surveyed the people and the priests, and of the sons of Levi I did not find there.
And I sent to Eliezer, Ariel, Shemayah, Elnathan, Yariv, Elnathan, Nasan, Zecharyah, and Meshullam, the heads, and Yoiarib and Elnathan, the wise men.

And I commanded them to [go to] Iddo, the head in the place Casiphia, and I put words into their mouth to speak to Iddo [and] to Ahiv, who were settled in the place Casiphia to bring us servants for the House of our Elokim.

And they brought us according to the hand of our Elokim, which was good over us, a man of intellect, of the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi, the son of Yisroel, and Sherevyah and his sons and his brothers, eighteen.
And Chashavyah, and with him Yeshayah of the sons of Merari, his brothers and their sons, twenty.
And of the Nethinim, whom King Dovid had appointed, and the chiefs, for the service of the Leviim, Nethinim [were] two hundred and twenty — all of them specified by name.
And I proclaimed there a fast by the river Ahava, to fast before our Elokim, to beseech Him for a straight way for us and for our children and for all our belongings.

For I was ashamed to request of the king an army and horsemen to aid us from enemies on the way, for we had said to the king, "The hand of our Elokim is upon all who seek Him for good, and His power and His wrath are upon all who forsake Him."
And we fasted and beseeched our Elokim concerning this, and He accepted our prayer.
And I separated twelve of the chiefs of the priests, Sherevyah, Chashavyah, and with them, ten of their brothers.
And I weighed out for them the silver and the gold and the vessels, the offering for the House of our Elokim, which the king, his advisers, his chiefs, and all Yisroel who were present, had offered.
And I weighed out upon their hands six hundred and fifty talents of silver, and one hundred silver vessels by talents, [and] one hundred talents of gold.
And twenty sprinkling bowls of gold of one thousand darics, and two vessels of fine golden copper, precious as gold.
And I said to them, "You are holy to Havayah, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and the gold are a donation to Havayah Elokim of your forefathers.

Hasten and guard [them] until you weigh [them] out before the chiefs of the priests and the Leviim, and the chiefs of the fathers' [houses] of Yisroel in Yerushalayim, [to deposit in] the chambers of the House of Havayah."
And the priests and the Leviim received by weight the silver, the gold, and the vessels, to bring to Yerushalayim for the House of our Elokim.

Then we traveled from the river Ahava on the twelfth of the first month to go to Yerushalayim, and the hand of our Elokim was upon us, and He saved us from the clutches of the enemy and those who lie in wait on the way.
And we came to Yerushalayim and stayed there three days.

And on the fourth day, the silver, the gold, and the vessels were weighed in the House of our Elokim onto the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriyah the priest, and with him Elazar the son of Pinchas, and with them Yosevad the son of Yeshua, and Noadyah the son of Binnui, the Leviim.
Everything was counted and weighed and the entire weight was written at that time.

Those coming from captivity, the people of the exile, offered up burnt offerings to the Elokim of Yisroel, twelve bulls for all Yisroel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve he-goats for sin-offerings, all this was a burnt offering to Havayah.
And they gave the king's decrees to the satraps of the king and the governors of the land beyond the river, and they exalted the people and the House of Elokim.

And when these were completed, the chiefs approached me, saying "The people of Yisroel, the priests, and the Leviim were not separated from the peoples of the lands, like the abominations of the Kena'anim, the Chitim, the Perizzim, the Yevusim, the Ammonim, the Moavim, the Mitzrim, and the Emorim.

For they have taken of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, and the holy seed has become mingled with the peoples of the lands, and the hand of the chiefs and the deputies was first in this treachery."
And when I heard [of] this matter, I rent my garment and my robe, and I tore the hair of my head and my beard, and I sat bewildered.
And all those who hastened at the words of the Elokim of Yisroel gathered to me on account of the treachery of the community of the exiles, and I sat bewildered until the evening offering.
And at the [time of] the evening offering, I arose from my fast with the rent condition of my garment and my robe, and I kneeled on my knees and spread my palms to Havayah, my Elokim.
And I said, "O my Elokim, I am ashamed and embarrassed to lift up my face to You, my Elokim, for our iniquities have increased over our heads, and our guilt has grown up to the heavens.

Since the days of our forefathers, we are in great guilt until this day, and because of our iniquities, we were delivered — we, our kings, our priests-into the hands of the kings of the lands by the sword, in captivity, and with plunder and with shame-facedness as of this day.

And now, for a short moment, favor has been granted by Havayah our Elokim, to leave us a remnant and to give us a peg in His holy place, so that our Elokim may enlighten our eyes and grant us a little life in our servitude.

For we are slaves, and in our servitude our Elokim has not forsaken us, and He has extended loving-kindness upon us before the kings of Paras, to give us life, to exalt the House of our Elokim and to erect its ruins, and to give us a fence in Yehudah and in Yerushalayim.
And now, what shall we say, O Elokim, after this, for we have forsaken Your commandments,

Which You have commanded by Your servants the prophets, saying, 'The land that you are coming to inherit is an unclean land because of the uncleanliness of the peoples of the lands, by their abominations with which they filled it from end to end with their uncleanliness.

And now, you shall not give your daughters to their sons, neither shall you take their daughters for your sons, and you shall not seek their peace nor their prosperity to eternity, in order that you become strong and eat the goodness of the land, and you shall cause your children to inherit it to eternity.'

And after all that has come upon us because of our evil deeds and because of our great guilt, because You our Elokim, have punished us less than our inquities deserve, and You have given us a remnant such as this.
If we revert to breaking Your commandments to intermarrying with these abominable peoples, will You not be wroth with us until destruction without remnant or escape?
O Havayah Elokim of Yisroel, You are righteous, for we are left a remnant as of this day; behold we are before You in our guilt, for we cannot stand before You because of this."

And when Ezra prayed and confessed, weeping and prostrating himself before the House of Elokim, a very large assemblage of Yisroel, men, women, and children, gathered to him, for the people wept with much weeping.

And Shechanyah, the son of Yechiel, of the sons of Eilam, raised his voice and said to Ezra, "We have betrayed our Elokim, and we have taken in foreign wives of the peoples of the land, but now there is hope for Yisroel concerning this.

And now, let us make a covenant with our Elokim to cast out all the wives and their offspring, by the counsel of the Master and those who hasten to [perform] the commandment of our Elokim, and according to the Law it shall be done.
Rise, for the matter is incumbent upon you, and we are with you; be strong and do!"
Then Ezra rose and adjured the chiefs of the priests, the Leviim, and all Yisroel to do according to this matter, and they swore.

Then Ezra rose from before the House of Elokim, and he went to the chamber of Yehochanan the son of Eliashib. [When] he went there, he neither ate bread nor drank water, because he was mourning over the treachery of the community of the exiles.
And they issued a proclamation in Yehudah and Yerushalayim to all the people of the community of the exiles to assemble to Yerushalayim.
And whoever does not come by three days according to the counsel of the chiefs and the elders all his property shall be confiscated, and he shall be separated from the congregation of the exile.

And all the people of Yehudah and Binyamin assembled to Yerushalayim by three days; that is the ninth month, on the twentieth of the month, and all the people stayed in the broad plaza of the House of Elokim, quaking over the matter and because of the rains.
And Ezra the priest arose and said to them, "You have dealt treacherously, and you have taken in foreign wives to add to Yisroel's guilt.
And now, confess to Havayah, the Elokim of your forefathers, and do His will, and separate from the peoples of the land and from the foreign wives."
Then the entire congregation replied and said in a loud voice: "Yes! We must do as you say!
But the people are many, and it is the rainy season, and there is no strength to remain outside, and the work is not for one day and not for two, for we have sinned very much in this matter.

Let our chiefs remain now with the entire congregation, and whoever is in our cities who took in foreign wives shall come at appointed times and with them the elders of every city and its judges, until we avert the burning anger of our Elokim from us until this matter [is concluded]."
Only Yonasan, the son of Asahel, and Yachzeyah, the son of Tikvah, stood up against this, and Meshullam and Shabbathai the Levi supported them.

The people of the exile did so. Ezra the priest [and certain] men, heads of the fathers' houses after the house of their fathers, separated themselves, all of them [known] by name, and they convened on the first day of the tenth month to investigate the matter.
And they completed everything concerning the men who had brought in foreign women, until the first day of the first month.
And it was found of the sons of the priests who brought in foreign women, of the sons of Yeshua, the son of Yehotzadak, and his brothers: Maaseyah, Eliezer, Yariv, and Gedalyah.
And they advised them to cast out their wives, and the guilty ones [to bring] a ram for their guilt.
And of the sons of Immer: Chanani and Zevadyah.
And of the sons of Harim: Maasyah, Eliyahu, Shemayah, Yechiel, and Uziyah.
And of the sons of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseyah, Yishmael, Nethanel, Yozabad, and Elasah.
And of the Leviim: Yozabad, Shimi, and Kelajah — he is Kelita-Pesachyah, Yehudah, and Eliezer.
And of the singers: Eliashib; and of the gatekeepers: Shalum, Telem, and Uri.
And of Yisroel, of the sons of Parosh: Ramyah, Iziyah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Elazar, Malchijah, and Benayahu.
And of the sons of Eilam: Matanyah, Zecharyah, Yechiel, Abdi, Yeremos, and Eliyahu.
And of the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Matanyah, Yeremos, Zabad, and Aziza.
And of the sons of Bebai: Yehochanan, Chananyah, Zabbai, [and] Athlai.
And of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adayah, Yashuv, Sheal, and Ramos.
And of the sons of Pahath-Moav: Adna and Chelal; Benayahu, Maaseyah, Matanyah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Menasheh.
And of the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Ishijah, Malchijah, Shemayah, Shimon.
Binyamin, Malluch, [and] Shemaryah.
Of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Yeremai, Menasheh, [and] Shimi.
Of the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram, and Uel.
Benayahu, Bedeyah, Cheluhu.
Vanyah, Meremoth, Elyashib.
Matanyah, Mattenai, and Yaasai.
Bani, Binnui, Shimi.
Shelemyah, Nasan, Adayah.
Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai.
Azarel, Shelemyah, Shemaryah.
Shalum, Amaryah, and Yosef.
Of the sons of Nebo: Yeiel, Matisyah, Zabad, Zebina, Yadai, Yoel, and Benayah.
All these had taken foreign wives, and some of them had wives by whom they had children.
